principles.rule: Keep HTTP/request orchestration in routes, durable persistence in db, provider/network concerns behind services/integrations/llm, and retrieval behavior in rag. Do not introduce cross-layer shortcuts when an existing seam can own the behavior.

Pages compose screens, hooks own state and async orchestration, lib owns transport and pure helpers, and components own UI behavior. Avoid moving network/state orchestration into presentation components when an existing hook or lib seam fits.
Prefer stable, deep modules and reuse existing seams before adding parallel helpers, one-off abstractions, cross-layer shortcuts, or speculative extension points.

Preserve separation between builder reasoning and independent validation. Builder artifacts may propose evidence; authoritative validation must recompute or independently verify security-critical facts.

migrations.direction: Move new capability-specific persistence toward focused repository modules. Avoid unrelated growth in the monolithic repository.
When materially extending LLM behavior, separate provider transport/client concerns from chat orchestration rather than growing the provider module as a general service hub.
Keep tool contracts and focused implementations separable. Avoid growing one central tool module with unrelated retrieval/application concerns.
Keep the route as the HTTP/SSE boundary and move reusable business or orchestration logic behind service, rag, llm, or persistence seams when new behavior would otherwise enlarge the route.
Substantial new state, networking, or orchestration behavior should move into focused hooks/lib seams rather than further enlarging the large UI components.
Keep the repo-owned runtime as a thin coordinator. New substantial builder, validator, holdout, or recovery behavior should move into focused kernel modules instead of enlarging runtime.py.

debt.note: Large persistence hub; any touched change must not increase its byte footprint and new unrelated capability should prefer a focused repository module.
Provider transport and orchestration are concentrated; any touched change must not increase the file footprint and material extension should improve separation.
Tool hub is already broad; any touched change must not increase its footprint or add unrelated responsibilities.
Large route; any touched change must not increase its footprint and reusable orchestration belongs outside the HTTP boundary.
Large components are tolerated as inherited debt, but touched changes must not increase their combined footprint; material state/network behavior should converge toward hooks/lib.
The rewritten control plane begins as a cohesive coordinator, but further substantial responsibilities must move into focused builder/validator/recovery modules rather than growing runtime.py.
